newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Philips Calcutta unit on strike.
newsitem.headline: India's Philips Calcutta unit on strike.

text.p: Employees of electronics firm Philips India Ltd went on a two-day strike in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta after a prolonged wage dispute, the company said.
It said in a statement three wage settlements (in New Delhi, Bombay and three Calcutta plants) have not yet been concluded despite negotiations over the last 12-18 months.
Philips said the strike -- on Thursday and Friday -- was "an attempt to coerce the management to give in to their demands."
Philips said it had offered Calcutta employees an average 20 percent wage increase but employee unions had rejected the offer and had demanded about 25 percent more than the offer.
But Kiran Mehta, president of the Philips Employees Union in Bombay said the wage hike offered had been lower.
"The company has never given any firm offer but it is hovering around 10 percent or so," Mehta told Reuters.
He said the unions were demanding a 15 percent wage hike in Bombay and New Delhi, and a 20 percent raise for employees in Calcutta.

Philips said the basic principle that the company is trying to establish in these wage negotiations is that, "wage increases can no longer be passed on to the customer through price increases and has to be offset by higher productivity, flexibility and multi-skilling."
Mehta said staff costs as a percentage of turnover had fallen sharply since the eighties and this should be kept in mind while considering the hike in wages.
Philips India Ltd is 51 percent owned by Philips N.V. of Holland.
